title: Tokens, Sequences & Objectives
description: Study what next-token prediction learns, causal masking and shifted targets, cross entropy and perplexity, and context length and positional limits. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: What next-token prediction learns
lessons.description: Construct three prefixes where an identical final phrase requires different next tokens.
lessons.conceptOverview: A language model assigns a distribution to the next token conditional on a prefix. Training compares that distribution with the observed continuation. This objective can teach useful patterns without directly guaranteeing truth, reasoning skill, or calibrated confidence.
lessons.whyItMatters: The model estimates a conditional token distribution rather than consulting a guaranteed fact table.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: A language model assigns a distribution to the next token conditional on a prefix. Training compares that distribution with the observed continuation. This objective can teach useful patterns without directly guaranteeing truth, reasoning skill, or calibrated confidence.

sections.title: Concept
sections.content: A language model assigns a distribution to the next token conditional on a prefix. Training compares that distribution with the observed continuation. This objective can teach useful patterns without directly guaranteeing truth, reasoning skill, or calibrated confidence.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: The prefix 'The capital is' supports many continuations depending on the preceding context; a fluent continuation can still be false.

sections.title: Practice & verification
sections.content: Construct three prefixes where an identical final phrase requires different next tokens. Write down your reasoning and check it against the concept before continuing.

keyTakeaways: The model estimates a conditional token distribution rather than consulting a guaranteed fact table.
commonMistakes: A high-probability continuation is necessarily a verified fact.

lessons.title: Causal masking and shifted targets
lessons.description: Write the input-target pairs and causal mask for a five-token sequence.
lessons.conceptOverview: Decoder training predicts every next token in parallel while a causal mask prevents each position from seeing future input tokens. Targets are shifted relative to inputs. Padding and special-token positions need an explicit loss policy.
lessons.whyItMatters: Shift targets and block future-token attention to preserve the prediction task.

lessons.title: Cross entropy and perplexity
lessons.description: Calculate the mean negative log likelihood for target probabilities 0.5 and 0.25.
lessons.conceptOverview: Cross entropy penalizes low probability on the observed token. Perplexity is the exponential of average negative log likelihood when natural logarithms are used. Compare perplexity only under compatible tokenization, data, and evaluation conventions; it is not a universal task-quality score.

lessons.title: Context length and positional limits
lessons.description: Design a test that moves the same evidence between the beginning, middle, and end of a context.
lessons.conceptOverview: A context limit constrains the total tokens processed in an invocation. Position encoding, attention behavior, and training distribution also affect useful long-context performance. Fitting text inside a advertised window does not mean every detail can be retrieved reliably.
lessons.whyItMatters: Measure effective evidence use rather than only checking whether tokens fit.
